title: CASE WHEN expressions — conditional logic in SQL
description: Branching logic inside queries for categorization, pivoting, and conditional aggregation. Interview: 'Write a query that labels orders as Small/Medium/Large based on total amount.'

children.title: Simple and searched CASE expressions
children.description: CASE value WHEN ... THEN ... vs CASE WHEN condition THEN ...; order matters for overlapping conditions. Interview: 'What's the difference between simple and searched CASE? When do you need each?'

children.title: Nested CASE and COALESCE/NULLIF alternatives
children.description: When CASE can be replaced by COALESCE or NULLIF for simpler expressions. Interview: 'Rewrite this nested CASE using COALESCE — is it always equivalent?'

children.title: Conditional aggregation with CASE inside SUM/COUNT
children.description: COUNT(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 END) for pivoting without GROUP BY extension. Interview: 'Count active and inactive users per month in a single query using CASE inside aggregate.'

title: Set operations — UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT
description: Combining result sets from multiple queries; UNION ALL vs UNION (deduplicating), INTERSECT for common rows, EXCEPT for set difference. Interview: 'Find customers who purchased in both January and February using set operations.'

children.title: UNION ALL vs UNION — performance and correctness
children.description: UNION ALL preserves duplicates and is faster; UNION deduplicates which requires a sort or hash. Interview: 'When would UNION be slower than UNION ALL? How do you decide?'

children.title: INTERSECT and EXCEPT — set membership and difference
children.description: INTERSECT returns rows present in both; EXCEPT returns rows in first but not second. Interview: 'Find products that were ordered last year but not this year using EXCEPT.'

children.title: Column compatibility rules and ORDER BY placement
children.description: Same number of columns, compatible types; ORDER BY applies to the final result only. Interview: 'Can you UNION a VARCHAR column with an INTEGER column? What about ORDER BY on the second SELECT?'

title: NULL semantics — three-valued logic in SQL
description: NULL = NULL is NULL (not TRUE), NULL in aggregates, COALESCE/NULLIF. Interview: 'Why does WHERE col = NULL return no rows? How do you properly check for NULLs?'

children.title: Three-valued logic — TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN in comparisons
children.description: NULL propagates through most expressions; only IS NULL/IS NOT NULL test it directly. Interview: 'What is the result of NULL AND TRUE, NULL OR FALSE, NOT NULL?'

children.title: COALESCE, NULLIF, and GREATEST — working with NULLs in expressions
children.description: COALESCE returns first non-null; NULLIF returns null on equality; GREATEST skips nulls. Interview: 'Use COALESCE to provide default values and NULLIF to convert zero to null for division.'

children.title: NULL handling in DISTINCT, ORDER BY, and UNIQUE constraints
children.description: NULLs are considered distinct for DISTINCT, sorted at end in ASC. Interview: 'Does a UNIQUE constraint allow multiple NULLs? Does it depend on the database?'

title: GROUP BY with HAVING — aggregation filtering
description: Filtering grouped results vs WHERE filtering. Interview: 'Find all customers who placed more than 5 orders in the last 30 days — explain your WHERE vs HAVING logic.'

children.title: WHERE vs HAVING — filtering before vs after aggregation
children.description: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Interview: 'Can you use aggregate functions in WHERE? Why or why not?'

children.title: GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE for multi-level summaries
children.description: Generating subtotals and grand totals in a single query. Interview: 'Write a query that produces a sales summary with subtotals per region and a grand total.'

children.title: GROUP BY ordinal position and column alias usage
children.description: Using column positions or aliases in GROUP BY. Interview: 'Is SELECT a, b, SUM(c) FROM t GROUP BY 1, 2 equivalent to GROUP BY a, b? Are there caveats?'

children.title: FILTER clause — conditional aggregation within a single query
children.description: Apply aggregate functions to subsets of rows without subqueries. Interview: 'Count total orders and count orders over $100 in a single query using FILTER.'

title: Database constraints — PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, EXCLUDE
description: Enforcing data integrity at the database level. Interview: 'How would you prevent overlapping time ranges for a resource booking system at the DB level?'

children.title: PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints — enforcement and index creation
children.description: Both create unique indexes; PK is NOT NULL + UNIQUE; multiple UNIQUE constraints allowed. Interview: 'What indexes are automatically created when you define a PRIMARY KEY vs a UNIQUE constraint?'

children.title: CHECK constraints — custom business rules at the database level
children.description: Enforce value ranges, cross-column logic, and format requirements. Interview: 'Write a CHECK constraint ensuring end_date is always after start_date.'

children.title: EXCLUDE constraints — preventing overlapping ranges
children.description: Uses GiST index to enforce non-overlapping geometric or range types. Interview: 'Use an EXCLUDE constraint to prevent double-booking a room in a reservation system.'

children.title: Deferrable constraints and ON CONFLICT (UPSERT) patterns
children.description: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, constraint deferral within transactions. Interview: 'Write an upsert that inserts or updates depending on a unique constraint conflict.'

title: Foreign key cascades — ON DELETE/UPDATE actions
description: CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT, RESTRICT, NO ACTION. Interview: 'What happens when you delete a parent row with ON DELETE CASCADE vs RESTRICT? Which do you prefer in production?'

children.title: ON DELETE CASCADE — automatic child deletion and its risks
children.description: Deletes propagate to children; can cause unintended mass deletions. Interview: 'When is CASCADE dangerous? Give an example where it caused a production incident.'

children.title: ON DELETE SET NULL vs SET DEFAULT — preserving child records
children.description: Nullifies or resets FK columns instead of deleting; requires nullable or default column. Interview: 'When would you choose SET NULL over CASCADE for a foreign key?'

children.title: RESTRICT vs NO ACTION — blocking parent deletion
children.description: Both prevent deletion of referenced parents; RESTRICT checks immediately, NO ACTION at commit. Interview: 'What's the difference between RESTRICT and NO ACTION? When does it matter?'

title: Schema design — normalization (1NF through 3NF) and when to denormalize
description: Knowing normal forms and when production systems deviate for performance. Interview: 'When would you denormalize a 3NF schema? Give a concrete example.'

children.title: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF — progressive normalization rules
children.description: Atomic values, no partial dependencies, no transitive dependencies. Interview: 'Explain each normal form with a concrete example. What anomalies does each prevent?'

children.title: When to denormalize — read-heavy workloads and query simplification
children.description: Materializing computed columns, pre-joining for dashboards, controlled redundancy. Interview: 'Your dashboard query joins 6 tables and is slow — how do you denormalize to fix it?'

children.title: Star schema and snowflake schema for analytical workloads
children.description: Fact tables, dimension tables, and query patterns. Interview: 'Design a star schema for an e-commerce order analytics system.'

children.title: Choice between JSONB columns vs relational normalization
children.description: When semi-structured storage makes sense vs strict normalization. Interview: 'Your client sends varying payload shapes — when would you use JSONB columns instead of separate tables?'

title: SQL injection prevention and parameterized queries
description: Understanding how injection works and defense-in-depth strategies. Interview: 'How does parameterized query execution prevent SQL injection? What about dynamic identifiers?'

children.title: Parameterized queries — how binding prevents injection
children.description: Separating SQL structure from data at the protocol level; no string interpolation. Interview: 'Why does a parameterized query prevent injection even if the parameter contains SQL syntax?'

children.title: Stored procedures as a defense layer — and their limitations
children.description: Procedures can restrict direct table access but don't prevent injection if they use dynamic SQL internally. Interview: 'Does using stored procedures automatically prevent SQL injection? Why or why not?'

title: Data types and their performance implications
description: INTEGER vs BIGINT vs SMALLINT, VARCHAR vs TEXT, TIMESTAMP vs TIMESTAMPTZ, SERIAL vs GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY. Interview: 'Why does choosing the wrong data type hurt performance? Give two examples.'

children.title: Integer types — SMALLINT, INTEGER, BIGINT and when each is appropriate
children.description: Storage size, index efficiency, and overflow risks. Interview: 'When would SMALLINT be insufficient? What's the max value for INTEGER?'

children.title: Character types — CHAR vs VARCHAR vs TEXT and collation effects
children.description: Fixed vs variable length, performance implications for indexing and comparisons. Interview: 'Is VARCHAR(255) faster than TEXT? Does it matter for indexes?'

children.title: UUID vs serial/identity for primary keys — tradeoffs
children.description: Index fragmentation, insert performance, distribution. Interview: 'Why are random UUIDs bad for B-tree primary keys? What alternatives exist?'

children.title: Date/time timezone handling and interval arithmetic
children.description: TIMESTAMPTZ storage, session timezone, date_trunc, age(). Interview: 'Two users in Berlin and Tokyo insert the same timestamp — is it stored the same? How do you compare across timezones?'

title: FULL JOIN, CROSS JOIN, and non-equi joins
description: Completing the join vocabulary beyond INNER and LEFT/RIGHT. FULL JOIN for symmetric set comparisons, CROSS JOIN for cartesian products, theta joins for range-based matching. Interview: 'Write a FULL JOIN to compare this quarter vs last quarter revenue side-by-side.'

children.title: FULL JOIN — symmetric comparison of two result sets
children.description: Returns all rows from both sides; NULLs fill gaps. Interview: 'Find customers who ordered in January but not February, and vice versa, in a single query.'

children.title: Non-equi joins — joining on ranges, inequalities, and complex conditions
children.description: JOIN ON a.start < b.end AND a.end > b.start for overlapping ranges. Interview: 'Write a non-equi join to find all booking overlaps for a given room.'

children.title: NATURAL JOIN and USING — shorthand and their pitfalls
children.description: NATURAL JOIN auto-matches on all same-named columns; USING simplifies syntax but hides which columns joined. Interview: 'Why do many style guides forbid NATURAL JOIN?'

title: Common SQL anti-patterns and how to fix them
description: SELECT *, excessive JOINs, N+1 queries, SELECT in SELECT, missing WHERE on UPDATE/DELETE. Interview: 'Here are 5 queries — identify the anti-patterns and propose fixes.'

children.title: SELECT * — why explicit column lists are always preferred
children.description: Prevents index-only scans, wastes I/O, breaks on schema changes. Interview: 'Why is SELECT * harmful? Give three concrete consequences.'

children.title: Missing WHERE on UPDATE/DELETE — the accidental full-table mutation
children.description: Without WHERE, every row is affected; can lock the table for minutes. Interview: 'A developer ran UPDATE without WHERE — what's the immediate damage and recovery plan?'

children.title: Over-normalization and over-normalized schemas causing join-heavy queries
children.description: Identifying when a schema is too normalized for its workload. Interview: 'Your query joins 8 tables to render a single page — how do you address this architecturally?'

children.title: Subqueries in SELECT (scalar subqueries) — N+1 disguised as SQL
children.description: Each row triggers a separate subquery execution; replace with JOIN or window function. Interview: 'Rewrite this SELECT with correlated subqueries as a single JOIN.'

title: Correlated subqueries vs JOINs — performance and correctness
description: When a correlated subquery executes per-row vs a single JOIN pass. Interview: 'Rewrite this correlated subquery as a JOIN. When would you NOT want to?'

children.title: How correlated subqueries execute — per-row evaluation cost
children.description: The inner query runs once per outer row; planner may not always decorrelate. Interview: 'Why is a correlated subquery sometimes slower than a JOIN? When is it actually better?'

children.title: EXISTS vs IN vs ANY/ALL — semantics and planner behavior
children.description: NULL handling differences, how the planner optimizes each. Interview: 'Why can EXISTS return different results than IN when dealing with NULLs?'

children.title: Rewriting correlated subqueries as JOINs or lateral joins
children.description: When the planner can decorrelate vs when manual rewrite is needed. Interview: 'Rewrite this correlated subquery as a JOIN — what conditions need to hold for correctness?'

title: Query optimization — rewriting for better performance
description: Replacing OR with UNION ALL, avoiding SELECT *, LIMIT without ORDER BY, using EXISTS instead of COUNT. Interview: 'Here's a slow query — rewrite it to be faster without changing the schema.'

children.title: Replacing OR conditions with UNION ALL for index efficiency
children.description: OR on different columns prevents index use; UNION ALL with separate index-friendly predicates. Interview: 'Rewrite this OR query to use indexes on both columns.'

children.title: Avoiding SELECT * — why explicit column lists matter
children.description: Wasted I/O, preventing index-only scans, network overhead. Interview: 'Why is SELECT * harmful on a table with a covering index?'

children.title: Avoiding the n+1 query problem in application code
children.description: Eager loading, batch fetching, and how ORMs generate queries. Interview: 'Your ORM is generating 1 query per row — how do you fix it?'

children.title: Pagination strategies — OFFSET/LIMIT vs keyset pagination
children.description: OFFSET degrades at high page numbers, keyset uses WHERE on indexed column. Interview: 'Why is OFFSET 1000000 slow? How does keyset pagination solve it?'

title: Window Functions — ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE
description: Understand the differences between row numbering and ranking semantics, when to use each, and how OVER clause partitioning works. Interview: 'Find the second highest salary per department — write two solutions using different window functions.'

children.title: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK — when to use each
children.description: Distinguish when rows need unique assignment vs handling ties. Interview: 'Find the second highest salary per department using both RANK and DENSE_RANK — what's the difference in result?'

children.title: NTILE for percentile and quartile splitting
children.description: Divide ordered rows into N equal buckets for statistical analysis. Interview: 'Split users into quartiles by revenue and label each quartile.'

children.title: OVER clause with PARTITION BY — row numbering per group
children.description: How partitioning scopes window function results to logical groups. Interview: 'Rank employees within each department by salary — explain how PARTITION BY interacts with ORDER BY.'

children.title: Window functions with FETCH/NEXT clauses and frame specifications
children.description: ROWS BETWEEN, RANGE BETWEEN, UNBOUNDED PRECEDING/FOLLOWING, CURRENT ROW. Interview: 'What's the difference between ROWS and RANGE frames? When would a range frame give a different result?'

title: CTEs (WITH clause) and Recursive CTEs
description: Non-recursive CTEs for readability and decomposition; recursive CTEs for hierarchical/graph traversal. Interview: 'Write a recursive CTE to find all subordinates under a manager in an org chart table.'

children.title: Non-recursive CTEs — breaking complex queries into readable blocks
children.description: Use WITH to decompose multi-step logic, referencing prior CTEs sequentially. Interview: 'Rewrite this nested subquery as a CTE — explain how readability and maintainability improve.'

children.title: Recursive CTEs — anchor member, recursive member, and UNION ALL
children.description: Structure the base case and recursive step for tree/graph traversal. Interview: 'Write a recursive CTE to traverse an org chart and return each employee with their hierarchy level.'

children.title: Recursive CTE termination conditions and cycle detection
children.description: Preventing infinite recursion using SEARCH or CYCLE clauses (PostgreSQL 14+). Interview: 'How do you prevent infinite loops in a recursive CTE? What happens if you omit the termination condition?'

children.title: CTEs vs subqueries vs temp tables — performance implications
children.description: Materialization behavior differs across databases (PostgreSQL inlines CTEs by default, SQL Server materializes). Interview: 'When would you choose a CTE over a subquery? When would you choose a temp table?'

title: Window functions for deduplication and gaps-and-islands
description: Using ROW_NUMBER to find duplicates, LAG to detect gaps in sequences. Interview: 'Find all consecutive date gaps in a bookings table where a room is unoccupied.'

children.title: Deduplication with ROW_NUMBER — keeping first or last occurrence
children.description: Partition by key, order by timestamp, filter where rn = 1. Interview: 'Write a query that keeps only the most recent record per user from a table with duplicates.'

children.title: LAG/LEAD/FIRST_VALUE/LAST_VALUE for time-series comparisons
children.description: Accessing values across rows without self-joins. Interview: 'Calculate month-over-month revenue growth rate from a transactions table.'

children.title: Gaps-and-islands: contiguous range detection
children.description: Subtract row_number from date to identify islands of consecutive values. Interview: 'Find all periods where a server was down continuously, given a table of incident timestamps.'

title: Cumulative sums and moving averages with window functions
description: Running totals, rolling windows, cumulative distributions. Interview: 'Write a query that returns a 7-day moving average of daily active users.'

children.title: Running totals with SUM() OVER (ORDER BY ... ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
children.description: Accumulate values row-by-row within a partition. Interview: 'Calculate a running total of daily sales partitioned by store.'

children.title: Moving averages with frame specifications — ROWS BETWEEN N PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
children.description: Rolling windows over N rows; handles gaps with RANGE for date-based windows. Interview: 'Write a 7-day moving average that handles missing dates gracefully.'

children.title: Cumulative distribution and percent_rank for statistical analysis
children.description: CUME_DIST, PERCENT_RANK, NTILE for relative positioning. Interview: 'Rank customers by lifetime value and assign percentile labels.'

title: Cartesian products, self-joins, and lateral joins (PostgreSQL)
description: Recognizing accidental cross joins, using LATERAL for row-by-row subquery evaluation. Interview: 'What's a lateral join? Give a use case where it's essential.'

children.title: Accidental Cartesian products — detecting and preventing cross joins
children.description: Missing JOIN condition produces m×n rows; EXPLAIN shows nested loop with no join filter. Interview: 'Your query returned 100M rows instead of 1000 — what likely went wrong?'

children.title: Self-joins — joining a table to itself for comparisons
children.description: Finding pairs, hierarchies, or gaps within the same table. Interview: 'Write a self-join to find all employees who earn more than their manager.'

children.title: LATERAL joins — row-by-row subquery evaluation
children.description: Subquery references outer columns; enables top-N-per-group without window functions. Interview: 'Use LATERAL to find the 3 most recent orders per customer.'

title: Pivot and unpivot patterns — crosstab aggregations
description: Transforming rows to columns and back for reporting. Interview: 'Write a query that produces a monthly revenue pivot table with months as columns.'

children.title: Manual pivot with CASE and GROUP BY
children.description: Use CASE inside SUM/COUNT to transform row values into columns. Interview: 'Pivot a sales table so each product category becomes a column with total revenue.'

children.title: PostgreSQL crosstab() from tablefunc extension
children.description: Built-in pivot function requiring tablefunc; row/column specification. Interview: 'When would you use crosstab() instead of manual CASE-based pivot?'

children.title: Unpivoting — converting columns back to rows with UNNEST or LATERAL
children.description: Expand JSON arrays or multiple columns into rows. Interview: 'Unpivot a table with columns mon, tue, wed into day/value rows.'

title: Materialized views — creation, REFRESH, and invalidation
description: Precomputed query results for dashboards and analytics. Interview: 'When would you use a materialized view instead of a regular view? How do you handle stale data?'

children.title: Creating materialized views — syntax, indexes, and refresh on first use
children.description: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW AS SELECT ...; data is snapshot at creation time. Interview: 'How does a materialized view differ from a regular view in PostgreSQL?'

children.title: REFRESH strategies — full refresh vs incremental approaches
children.description: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW rebuilds entirely; custom incremental refresh via triggers or logic. Interview: 'Your materialized view takes 30 minutes to refresh — how do you reduce downtime?'

children.title: Concurrent REFRESH and REFRESH strategies for live systems
children.description: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY requires unique index. Interview: 'How do you refresh a materialized view without blocking reads on a production system?'

title: Stored procedures, functions, and triggers in PostgreSQL
description: PL/pgSQL basics, when to use server-side logic vs application logic. Interview: 'When would you put business logic in a stored procedure versus the application layer?'

children.title: PL/pgSQL basics — variables, loops, conditionals, and error handling
children.description: Declaring variables, FOR loops, IF/ELSE, BEGIN/EXCEPTION blocks. Interview: 'Write a stored procedure that loops through rows and performs conditional updates.'

children.title: Functions vs procedures — volatility categories and calling conventions
children.description: VOLATILE, STABLE, IMMUTABLE; functions return values, procedures use CALL. Interview: 'What's the difference between a function and a procedure in PostgreSQL? When use each?'

children.title: Trigger design — BEFORE/AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE patterns
children.description: Audit logging, cascading updates, data validation at DB level. Interview: 'Design an audit trail using triggers that captures who changed what and when.'

children.title: Security — GRANT/REVOKE, row-level security (RLS)
children.description: Principle of least privilege, policies that filter rows per user. Interview: 'How would you implement row-level security so each tenant only sees their own data?'

title: Dynamic SQL safely — pg_ident_quote, identifier quoting
description: When you must interpolate identifiers (not values) and how to do it safely. Interview: 'You need a query with dynamic table names — how do you prevent injection when you can't parameterize identifiers?'

children.title: Identifier quoting with quote_ident() — preventing injection in DDL
children.description: Use quote_ident() for dynamic table/column names; parameterize values separately. Interview: 'Write a dynamic SQL query that safely interpolates a user-supplied table name.'

children.title: Dynamic SQL in PL/pgSQL — EXECUTE with USING for parameterized values
children.description: Build dynamic queries with EXECUTE ... USING to pass parameters safely. Interview: 'When would you use EXECUTE in PL/pgSQL vs a static query?'

title: Prepared statements and plan caching
description: PREPARE/EXECUTE in PostgreSQL, prepared statement protocols in drivers, plan cache invalidation. Interview: 'How do prepared statements improve performance? When can they hurt?'

children.title: PREPARE and EXECUTE in PostgreSQL — syntax and lifecycle
children.description: Server-side plan caching with parameter types; DEALLOCATE to free. Interview: 'Write a prepared statement for a parameterized SELECT and explain when the plan is reused.'

children.title: Plan cache invalidation — when prepared statements re-optimize
children.description: Schema changes, ANALYZE, and pg_stat_statements tracking. Interview: 'Your prepared statement suddenly got slow — what could have caused plan invalidation?'

children.title: Extended query protocol in PostgreSQL wire protocol
children.description: How drivers (libpq, JDBC) use Parse/Bind/Execute for parameterized queries. Interview: 'What happens at the protocol level when you run a parameterized query from a driver?'

title: JOIN algorithms — Nested Loop, Hash Join, Merge Join
description: Understand how the query planner chooses join strategies and when each is optimal. Interview: 'Explain when a hash join outperforms a merge join. What conditions favor a nested loop?'

children.title: Nested Loop Join — when small tables meet indexed lookups
children.description: Planner uses nested loop for small result sets or when inner table has an index on the join key. Interview: 'Under what conditions does the planner pick a nested loop over a hash join?'

children.title: Hash Join — building and probing for equi-joins on large tables
children.description: Planner builds hash table from smaller input, probes with larger. Memory spills to disk if needed. Interview: 'Explain the two phases of a hash join. When does it spill to temp files?'

children.title: Merge Join — sorted inputs and efficiency on pre-sorted data
children.description: Both inputs must be sorted on join key; efficient when indexes or ORDER BY already provide order. Interview: 'Why does merge join require sorted inputs? How does this affect index design?'

children.title: Index design for optimal JOIN performance
children.description: B-tree indexes on join columns, covering indexes, composite index column order. Interview: 'You have a slow JOIN between two million-row tables. Walk me through your index strategy.'

title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE — reading and interpreting query plans
description: Seq Scan vs Index Scan, cost estimates, actual vs estimated rows, filter selectivity. Interview: 'Here's an EXPLAIN output — where is the bottleneck and how would you fix it?'

children.title: Seq Scan vs Index Scan vs Index Only Scan — choosing the right scan type
children.description: When the planner falls back to sequential scan vs using an index vs returning directly from the index. Interview: 'Your EXPLAIN shows a Seq Scan on a 50M row table — what's your first move?'

children.title: Reading cost estimates and actual vs predicted row counts
children.description: How startup and total costs relate to I/O and CPU, when estimated rows diverge from actual. Interview: 'Your plan shows estimated 100 rows but actual is 500K — what went wrong?'

children.title: Identifying missing indexes from execution plans
children.description: Look for Seq Scan on large tables, Hash Join on large unindexed sets, Sort operations that could use an index. Interview: 'Your query plan shows a sequential scan on a 50M row table — what's your first move?'

children.title: Understanding cost units, buffer hits, and I/O in plans
children.description: How PostgreSQL reports shared buffers, temp files, and WAL. Interview: 'What does "Buffers: shared hit=1234" tell you about query performance?'

title: Index types — B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, Hash
description: Know which index type fits which workload (B-tree for equality/range, GIN for full-text/arrays, BRIN for append-only time-series). Interview: 'When would you choose a BRIN index over a B-tree? What are the tradeoffs?'

children.title: B-tree index — default workhorse for equality, range, and ORDER BY
children.description: Supports =, <, >, <=, >=, BETWEEN, LIKE 'abc%' patterns. Interview: 'What query patterns can a B-tree index accelerate? Which can it not?'

children.title: GIN index — full-text search, arrays, and JSONB containment
children.description: Inverted index for composite types; supports @>, tsvector/tsquery operators. Interview: 'When would you use a GIN index on a JSONB column vs a B-tree on a key path?'

children.title: GiST index — spatial data, range types, and nearest-neighbor searches
children.description: Generalized search tree for geometric, geographic, and range containment. Interview: 'How does a GiST index support KNN (nearest-neighbor) queries?'

children.title: BRIN index — block-range for append-only and time-series data
children.description: Stores min/max per block range; tiny size for naturally ordered data. Interview: 'Why is a BRIN index only 1KB on a 100M row table? When does it fail?'

title: Full-text search — tsvector, tsquery, and GIN indexes
description: PostgreSQL's built-in text search with lexeme matching, ranking, and language support. Interview: 'Implement full-text search with relevance ranking on a products table.'

children.title: tsvector and tsquery — tokenization and query construction
children.description: Converting text to lexemes, building boolean queries with AND/OR/NOT. Interview: 'What is a tsvector? How does to_tsvector differ from simple tokenization?'

children.title: Ranking with ts_rank and ts_rank_cd — relevance scoring
children.description: Cover density ranking, normalization flags, and custom weighting. Interview: 'How does ts_rank_cd differ from ts_rank? When would you prefer cover density?'

children.title: GIN vs GiST indexes for full-text search performance
children.description: GIN is faster for read-heavy workloads; GiST is smaller and faster to update. Interview: 'When would you choose GiST over GIN for full-text search indexing?'

children.title: phraseto_tsquery and websearch_to_tsquery — modern search syntax
children.description: Google-style query syntax, phrase matching, and prefix search. Interview: 'How does websearch_to_tsquery differ from plainto_tsquery? Give an example.'

title: Array operations and unnesting in PostgreSQL
description: Storing and querying array columns, unnesting to rows, array aggregation. Interview: 'How would you find all users who have a specific tag stored in an array column?'

children.title: Array column operations — containment, overlap, and indexing
children.description: @>, &&, <@ operators; GIN indexes on array columns. Interview: 'Write a query to find all products that contain both "organic" and "gluten-free" tags in an array column.'

children.title: UNNEST and LATERAL — expanding arrays into rows
children.description: Convert array elements to rows for joins and aggregation. Interview: 'Unnest a tags array column into individual rows and count occurrences of each tag.'

children.title: Array aggregation with array_agg and string_agg
children.description: Collecting grouped values into arrays or delimited strings. Interview: 'Aggregate all order IDs per customer into a single array column.'

title: JSONB operations — querying, indexing, and path extraction
description: Storing, querying, and indexing semi-structured JSON data in PostgreSQL. Interview: 'Write a query that finds all users where profile->>'age' > 30 using a GIN index.'

children.title: JSONB operators — ->, ->>, #>, #>>, @>, ?, and contains
children.description: Path extraction, containment checks, and key existence testing. Interview: 'What's the difference between -> and ->>? When would you use #> vs ->>'

children.title: GIN indexes on JSONB — containment and key/path indexing
children.description: jsonb_ops vs jsonb_path_ops; which supports which operators. Interview: 'When would you use jsonb_path_ops over the default jsonb GIN operator class?'

children.title: JSONB aggregation and transformation — jsonb_build_object, jsonb_agg
children.description: Building JSON from relational data, aggregating rows into JSON arrays. Interview: 'Convert a relational result set into a JSON array of objects for an API response.'

children.title: JSONB vs JSONB[] vs hstore — choosing the right semi-structured type
children.description: Performance, indexing, and query capability differences. Interview: 'When would you choose hstore over JSONB? What about JSONB[]?'

title: Transaction isolation levels — Read Uncommitted through Serializable
description: Understand dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads, and the practical tradeoffs. Interview: 'What isolation level does your application use and why? What problems does READ COMMITTED not protect against?'

children.title: Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantom reads — defining anomalies
children.description: Each anomaly type and which isolation levels prevent them. Interview: 'Explain the three read anomalies. Which isolation level prevents each?'

children.title: READ COMMITTED vs REPEATABLE READ vs SERIALIZABLE — practical tradeoffs
children.description: Default PostgreSQL is READ COMMITTED; when to escalate and performance cost. Interview: 'Why does PostgreSQL default to READ COMMITTED? When should you use SERIALIZABLE?'

children.title: MVCC internals — how PostgreSQL implements isolation
children.description: Tuple versioning, visibility checks, vacuum, wraparound. Interview: 'Explain how MVCC avoids locks for readers. What is transaction ID wraparound?'

children.title: SELECT FOR UPDATE / FOR SHARE — pessimistic locking patterns
children.description: Row-level locking to prevent lost updates. Interview: 'Write a query that atomically increments a counter while preventing concurrent lost updates.'

title: Index maintenance — REINDEX, fillfactor, and index-only scans
description: Keeping indexes healthy: bloat detection, REINDEX strategies, covering indexes for index-only scans. Interview: 'Your indexes are bloated — how do you detect and fix it without downtime?'

children.title: Index bloat detection — pg_stat_user_indexes and btree_check
children.description: Identifying bloated indexes using statistics and page-level inspection. Interview: 'How do you measure index bloat in PostgreSQL?'

children.title: REINDEX vs CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY — online rebuild strategies
